name: TeamStarWolf - PHP 8.4.27, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 Lab Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the lab-backed study of the two PHP flaws fixed in 8.4.27 (php2shell). Score 100: the vendor advisories and the CISA KEV listing support the technique directly. Score 50: the study's own mapping, labelled Inferred in its comment. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/PHP_8_4_27_CVES.md. No severity, prevalence or coverage is measured.

techniques.comment: Unauthenticated RCE over HTTP: validated against mod_php before application code runs (CVE-2026-109618, GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w, 2026-10-21) and against mod_php and PHP-FPM (CVE-2026-109619, GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp, 2026-10-21); both in CISA KEV from 2026-10-26. Sources: [1]; [2]; [16]; [18]; [39].
Inferred follow-on: the CISA alert (2026-10-21) tells defenders to watch for PHP worker processes launching shells. Sources: [17]; [40].

Inferred follow-on: the CISA alert (2026-10-21) names PHP workers downloading tools; TU Delft (Reported) counts 181 source IPs that sent code or a dropper by 2026-11-04. Sources: [17]; [23]; [45]; [49].
Inferred follow-on: a web shell is a common next step after RCE as the web worker account; no source opened for this study records one. Sources: [1]; [2]; [45]; [48].
Inferred side effect: the OOM producers of CVE-2026-109618 and the worker-state corruption of CVE-2026-109619 can end a PHP worker. Sources: [1]; [2]; [41].
